LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 3.1.1 ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Attentive listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Attentive listening, part of Strand 3 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to interrupt politely in a conversation? 2. How do we avoid conflict with wild animals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers the common conversational errors among speakers,

2. listen to a conversation on human-wildlife conflict between a game warden and a farmer (complaining about wild animals destroying crops in his or her farm),

3. identify conversational errors that may occur as a result of poor turn-taking and interrupting impolitely,

4. role play the conversation again while correcting the conversational errors made,

5. respond to questions from texts. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers the common conversational errors among speakers,
2. listen to a conversation on human-wildlife conflict between a game warden and a farmer (complaining about wild animals destroying crops in his or her farm),
3. identify conversational errors that may occur as a result of poor turn-taking and interrupting impolitely,
4. role play the conversation again while correcting the conversational errors made,
5. respond to questions from texts. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Attentive listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks engagingly with facts and examples when discussing with peers the

common conversational errors among speakers.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is developed as the learner analyses concept logically to identify conversational

errors that may occur as a result of poor turn-taking and interrupting impolitely.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with others to role play the conversation again while correcting the

conversational errors made.

• Respect: The learner displays patience when discussing with peers the common conversational errors among speakers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental education: This is instilled as the learner interacts with texts on wildlife and human-wildlife conflict.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the knowledge on human-wildlife conflict to the concept of wildlife conservation in Social Studies.
